title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated Copilot connectors read third-party data in real time
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing, availability controls and API examples are supported. Two small qualifications would clarify differences between Microsoft's authentication and write-action documentation; neither blocks publication.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) federated Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Federated Copilot Connectors in Microsoft 365 Copilot

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: November CY2026 is the roadmap target, not a committed release date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026", "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.quote: administrators retain full governance and control through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center

claims.quote: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that defines how AI applications communicate with data sources and tools.

claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
- Agents
- Cowork
- Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in Researcher.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector supplies the tools, Copilot can create, update or delete source data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.
claims.fix: After this description, add: "The broader connectors overview still calls federated connectors read-only, alongside a note that write actions were planned from early October 2026; this briefing follows the dedicated federated connectors page." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors, which says "Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back."

claims.claim: Learn does not identify which connectors and experiences belong specifically to this November government-cloud milestone.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "November" "2026" default rollout. Opened federated-connectors-overview, manage-federated-connectors and set-up-custom-federated-connectors; read June 2 release-notes excerpt. None maps the November government-cloud milestone to a connector or experience list.

claims.claim: The external source remains the system of record.
claims.quote: The source system remains the system of record

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Authenticated connector access and actions are limited to the user's existing source-system permissions.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.claim: Content returned from the source can reach the user's Copilot conversation.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.claim: Learn says administrators can audit federated connector activity in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The federated connector overview gives no audit navigation path or connector read/write event names.
claims.quote: Searched: federated Copilot connectors API enable staged rollout Graph write tools tenant wide disable sensitivity labels data policies Copilot Credits default general availability November 2026. Read federated-connectors-overview: Purview is named, but no audit path or event names.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default state of this particular GA arrival is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "default" "government"; "federated connectors" "November" "2026" default rollout. Read roadmap, overview, availability, custom setup and service description: conditional defaults, not a complete milestone default.

claims.claim: Microsoft-built connectors are available when their publisher option is selected and the user is in User access.
claims.quote: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when you select Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft in Agent and plugin access and include the user in User access.

claims.claim: External-publisher connectors require their publisher option or individual administrator enablement.
claims.quote: Connectors from external publishers are available only when you select Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers, or when an admin turns on the individual connector.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Connector documentation does not state connector-specific sensitivity-label enforcement on returned source data.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "sensitivity" "policies". Read federated-connectors-overview, custom setup and Purview ai-m365-copilot. Purview documents labels on files and data in use, but not connector-specific enforcement on returned MCP source records.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Connector documentation does not state connector-specific data-policy enforcement on returned source data.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "sensitivity" "policies". Read overview, custom setup, Purview ai-m365-copilot and plugin-type-connectors excerpt; Power Platform connector policies are documented for a distinct model, not returned federated source records.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documents auditing Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Like other activities, prompts and responses are captured in the unified audit log.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documents eDiscovery of Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Because user prompts and responses for AI apps are stored in a user's mailbox, you can create a case and use search when a user's mailbox is selected as the source for a search query.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview documents retention of Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Use retention policies to automatically retain or delete user prompts and responses for AI apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users sign in to each source using their own credentials.
claims.quote: User credentials, rather than admin credentials, are required to connect to any data source.
claims.fix: Qualify the sentence as "Where a source requires authentication, users sign in with their own credentials." In the impact rationale, replace "and sign in to the source" with "and, where required, sign in to the source". The cited custom setup page explicitly supports "No Auth" and says "Users don't need to authenticate"; the body already notes that exception.

claims.claim: The overview describes OAuth 2.0 securing connector access.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: The overview describes encrypted communication securing connector access.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: The source system enforces access permissions.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions.

claims.claim: Custom connectors support Microsoft Entra SSO, OAuth 2.0 and No Auth authentication choices.
claims.quote:
Custom federated connectors support three authentication methods. Choose the method that matches your data source.
Microsoft Entra SSO
OAuth 2.0
No Auth

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools initially require user approval and default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to Needs approval, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Always allow suppresses further prompts for that tool until the user changes the setting or its publisher changes the tool.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A publisher-added or changed write-capable tool is set to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools are part of the connector and are not enabled separately.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.claim: Publishers can add or change a connector's tools over time.
claims.quote: The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enable, disable and staging changes can take up to 10 minutes to propagate.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect across Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.claim: Users may need to refresh Copilot after configuration changes.
claims.quote: Users might need to refresh Copilot or start a new conversation.

claims.claim: An MCP server restricting source IP addresses must allow Microsoft 365 Copilot's static egress addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Static egress is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Static egress is enabled by default; no manifest flag is required.

claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "Package Management" Graph enable; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph federated connectors enable disable staging admin API. Read Package Management overview and block reference: no explicit federated connector applicability.

claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "write" "tenant" disable all tools; site:learn.microsoft.com "federated" "write" "tenant-wide". Read overview, availability, custom setup and TCM resources: blocking and approvals, but no tenant-wide write-only switch.

claims.quote: A setting you make on an individual connector takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting.

claims.claim: User access always applies even when an individual connector overrides publisher access.

claims.claim: Installed for and agent sharing settings do not apply to federated connectors.
claims.quote: Installed for and agent sharing settings don't apply to federated connectors.

claims.claim: TCM remediation and applyOnce are preview capabilities in Microsoft Graph beta, available only in the global service.

claims.claim: The TCM examples correctly select mode applyOnce to apply their inline baseline once.

claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.
